ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a blue shaded triangle, whose base is horizontal and labeled 29 cm, whose left side is a vertical side, and from the top to the right end is a slanted side. On the left there is also a pink dashed auxiliary right triangle, which shares the same vertical height with the blue triangle; the hypotenuse of this auxiliary triangle is labeled 13 cm, the horizontal base is labeled 6 cm, and a right angle is marked. Reasoning: First use the auxiliary right triangle to find the shared height h: h = sqrt(13^2 - 6^2) = sqrt(169 - 36) = sqrt(133) ≈ 11.5326 cm. The hypotenuse of the blue triangle is sqrt(29^2 + h^2) = sqrt(29^2 + 133) = sqrt(974) ≈ 31.2090 cm. Therefore the perimeter = 29 + 11.5326 + 31.2090 ≈ 71.7416 cm, which rounded to one decimal place is 71.7 cm.

raw_record.question_text: Find the perimeter of the triangle.

method.method_draft: Use the dashed auxiliary right triangle to determine the shared height, then apply the Pythagorean theorem to the shaded triangle. First read from the image that the shaded triangle has a horizontal base labeled 29 cm and a vertical left side; a dashed right triangle to the left shares this same vertical height, with hypotenuse 13 cm and horizontal leg 6 cm. Read from the text that the task is to find the perimeter of the triangle, meaning the shaded triangle. Compute the shared height as sqrt(13^2 - 6^2). Then compute the shaded triangle’s slanted side as sqrt(29^2 + height^2). Add base + height + slanted side, and round to one decimal to obtain 71.7.
